clinicalRisk: High bleeding risk from combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet effect.
recommendedAction: Avoid concurrent use unless specialist-directed; check INR and counsel on bleeding signs.

clinicalRisk: Severe GI bleeding risk when warfarin is combined with NSAIDs.
recommendedAction: Prefer paracetamol for analgesia; if NSAID unavoidable, gastroprotect and monitor closely.

clinicalRisk: Ciprofloxacin inhibits theophylline clearance, causing toxicity (tachycardia, seizures).
recommendedAction: Avoid combination or reduce theophylline dose and monitor serum levels.

clinicalRisk: Increased risk of lactic acidosis and renal impairment with NSAIDs or iodinated contrast.
recommendedAction: Hold metformin around contrast procedures; assess eGFR and hydration before NSAIDs.

clinicalRisk: Fluoroquinolones may alter glycemic control and warrant closer monitoring for lactic acidosis risk in metformin users with renal impairment.
recommendedAction: Monitor blood glucose and renal function; counsel on hypo/hyperglycemia symptoms during the antibiotic course.

clinicalRisk: Severe hyperkalemia from ACE inhibition plus potassium load or potassium-sparing diuretic.
recommendedAction: Check serum potassium promptly; avoid routine K+ supplements unless monitored.

clinicalRisk: Omeprazole may reduce CYP2C19 activation of clopidogrel and antiplatelet efficacy.
recommendedAction: Prefer pantoprazole or another non-interacting PPI if gastroprotection is required.

clinicalRisk: Additive GI bleeding risk from SSRI platelet effects plus NSAID mucosal injury.
recommendedAction: Consider gastroprotection; use lowest effective NSAID dose or alternative analgesia.

clinicalRisk: NSAIDs can reduce methotrexate clearance and precipitate acute toxicity.
recommendedAction: Avoid NSAIDs with high-dose MTX; monitor FBC/LFTs if co-prescription unavoidable.

clinicalRisk: Amiodarone raises digoxin levels with risk of bradycardia and digoxin toxicity.
recommendedAction: Halve digoxin dose when starting amiodarone; monitor digoxin level and ECG.

clinicalRisk: CYP3A4 inhibition markedly increases simvastatin exposure and rhabdomyolysis risk.
recommendedAction: Suspend simvastatin during macrolide/azole course; consider temporary statin hold.

clinicalRisk: Profound hypotension from combined PDE5 inhibitor and nitrate vasodilatation.
recommendedAction: Absolute contraindication — do not co-administer.

clinicalRisk: NSAIDs reduce lithium clearance and can cause lithium toxicity.
recommendedAction: Avoid NSAIDs; if needed, monitor lithium levels closely within days of change.

clinicalRisk: Serotonergic synergy raises risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
recommendedAction: Prefer non-serotonergic analgesia; counsel on agitation, tremor, and fever.

clinicalRisk: Additive negative chronotropy/inotropy with risk of bradycardia and heart block.
recommendedAction: Avoid oral verapamil with beta-blockers; monitor pulse and ECG if unavoidable.

clinicalRisk: Xanthine oxidase inhibition causes life-threatening myelosuppression.
recommendedAction: Reduce thiopurine dose to ~25% or avoid combination; monitor FBC closely.

clinicalRisk: Amiodarone potentiates warfarin anticoagulation and bleeding risk.
recommendedAction: Reduce warfarin dose empirically and intensify INR monitoring for weeks.

clinicalRisk: Heavy alcohol use with metformin increases lactic acidosis risk.
recommendedAction: Counsel on alcohol limits; hold metformin if acute illness or binge drinking.

clinicalRisk: Ciprofloxacin markedly elevates tizanidine levels causing hypotension and sedation.
recommendedAction: Contraindicated combination — choose alternative antibiotic or muscle relaxant.

clinicalRisk: Triple-whammy renal injury risk (ACEI + NSAID ± diuretic) with reduced GFR.
recommendedAction: Avoid chronic NSAIDs; check creatinine/electrolytes if short course required.

clinicalRisk: Strong CYP2D6 inhibition may reduce formation of active tamoxifen metabolite.
recommendedAction: Prefer a weak-CYP2D6 SSRI (e.g., sertraline/citalopram) if antidepressant needed.
